core_obligations: Construct p : X -> Y as the relative spectrum of the quasi-coherent O_Y-algebra A = (Sym-like direct sum of L_1^{tensor -a_1} tensor L_2^{tensor -a_2} over a_1, a_2 >= 0) modulo the ideal generated by all local sections st - t with t in a summand weighted a_1, a_2 > 0, and define s_i as the adjoints of L_i^{tensor -1} -> A = p_*O_X (proof lines 5858-5869).

Compute p on an affine open V = Spec(A) containing a point y after choosing trivializations z_i : O_V -> L_i^{tensor -1}|_V: the two sections glue to f = s(z_1 z_2) in A, which cuts out D, and p^{-1}(V) = Spec(B[z_1, z_2]/(z_1 z_2 - f)) (proof lines 5870-5880).

Read off all seven listed properties and the base-change compatibility from that local model: D_i is cut out by z_i, p is flat of relative dimension one, D_1 meet D_2 maps isomorphically to D and is the zero section of each D_i -> D (proof line 5880, 'since D_i is cut out by z_i everything is clear' plus the statement lines 5836-5851).
proof_roadmap: Define the graded algebra A as the quotient of the direct sum of the negative tensor powers of L_1 and L_2 by the ideal generated by st - t; let p : X -> Y be its relative spectrum (proof lines 5858-5864).
Define s_1 and s_2 as adjoints of the natural maps L_i^{tensor -1} -> A; then p^*s = s_1 tensor s_2 holds by construction (proof lines 5864-5866).

Work locally over an affine V = Spec(A) with trivializations z_i and f = s(z_1 z_2); the presentation Spec(B[z_1, z_2]/(z_1 z_2 - f)) gives flatness of relative dimension one, the two zero schemes D_i, the union and intersection identifications, and commutes with arbitrary base change (proof lines 5867-5880).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the zero scheme of one section of L_1 tensor L_2 can be resolved by a flat family of relative dimension one whose two relative Cartier divisors decompose it, with seven exact structural properties (statement lines 5821-5855, tag 0F97). The proof must build the family rather than invoke one: it forms a specific graded quotient algebra of the negative tensor powers of the two invertible modules, defines the two sections as adjoints of the resulting algebra maps, and then verifies flatness of relative dimension one, the scheme-theoretic union and intersection statements, and base change on a local presentation B[z_1, z_2]/(z_1 z_2 - f). Nothing here is a routine consequence of an existing theorem, so the claim is H2.
